impl:species-leafcutter.summary:
The Atta texana fungus-garden playstyle is built as a pure-sim species module, and the natural loop runs after hand-over with real workers and no cheats. Workers cut size-matched leaf fragments at plants and lawn herbage near the nest and carry them home. The fragments wait in the garden chamber's cache, are processed to pulp and planted as substrate. Garden growth follows the GDD 07 §6.4.2 law. Gardeners harvest staphylae, which feed the larvae and the queen.

Built and tested:
- Garden dynamics: health, contamination, climate tolerance, yield, the GDD 07 §6.4.3 states, and Escovopsis (outbreak, weeding, spread, quarantine through an `avoid` marker).
- Hygiene: refuse workers and waste hauling.
- Learned rejection of harmful plants, the garden-less state, and relocation and re-seeding with fungus pieces.
- Processing-chain bottleneck detection (`diag-at-chain`), plus `diag-garden`, `diag-at-substrate` and `diag-at-phorid`.
- Phorids with abstract hitchhikers, caste destiny and caste mix.
- Founding with the pellet (plant, hold until the garden is established, fertilisation, trophic eggs, and failure as `garden-lost`).
- Save/restore equality.

Not met:
- **Viability bar (addendum): not met on either archetype.** Only suburban-garden seed 2 passes the Winter-1 checks, and only on 4 first workers (range 8–14) with no leaf cutting at all. Three of the six seeds die in the founding cell even with the forced seal. Two of them were probed: the queen drowned (playground-park 1), or all larvae died of flooding in one tick (suburban-garden 3). Both are core flood rules, not this module.
- Where hand-over works (suburban-garden 1), the founding garden cannot grow. The 35 BU founding cell sits at about 28–30 °C after hand-over, so the temperature factor fT averages about 0.3. The architect never digs a deeper fungus chamber below 10 workers, so the garden stays at 0.6–0.7 GU, the founding minims die of old age, and the colony shrinks.

Three module fixes from this session:
- The queen's laying is held to the fungus in view. This removed a starvation and hygiene cascade: 29 brood hygiene deaths and 2.6 GD in rationing went to 0.
- Minims process leaves whenever no media works the gardens.
- Trophic egg eating is limited to the first clutch.

**Viability table** (`life.ts --species atta-texana --until winter`, naturalist; all runs needed life.ts's forced seal because the real founding fails):

| run | founding | first workers | Winter 1 | queen | workers at end (needs ≥0.8×first) | worker starvation deaths | longest stretch worse than lean | stores | viable |

| suburban-garden 1 (after fixes) | hand-over 4.6 GD | 9 | day 12 | alive | 4 (FAIL; 6 old-age) | 0 | 0 | 29 GD | NO |

Suburban-garden 2 through playground-park 3 ran with the laying hold and minim processing but before the trophic-eggs fix. I chose these two archetypes because the Atta site factors are sand 1.0 and loam 1.0, both lawn and garden archetypes have many leaf plants, and woodland-edge is humus (0.5).

**GDD 07 module status.**
- Done: §6.4.1 state; §6.4.2 growth, starvation, tending, yield, waste, contamination, climate fT and fRH, substrate quality, health recovery, relocation and re-seeding; §6.4.3 states; §6.4.4 hazard, growth, weeding, health, spread between gardens, quarantine spread ×0.1, refuse workers; §6.4.5 accept and reject; §6.4.6 stages 1–8 with bottleneck detection; §6.4.7 hitchhiker and phorid chance and parasitoid death; §6.4.8 founding garden; §6.4.9 garden-less; §6.4.11 diagnostics; §5.4.2 caste mix and destiny; §5.4.3 pellet founding.
- Partly done: §6.4.4 (no waste-through-garden spread, no quarantine waste routing, no inspect-card detection); §6.4.5 (no trail decay ×4); §6.4.9 (brood is not carried to a live garden, no epitaph cause); §6.4.12 player role (no fragment-size choice, no `hitchhikerEscort` directive wiring, no `externalHeap`); visuals (display items, not a renderer).
- Not done: air and vents (T3 stretch), co-founding (stretch), raid recovery (stretch), stridulation, the phorid-fly creature.

Core nest architect / balance nestTemplates: Atta never gets a fungus chamber below 10 workers (REQUIRED_TYPES worker gate), and the founding cell at about 35 BU runs 26–30 °C after hand-over (fT about 0.3), so the garden cannot grow. Atta needs a deeper fungus chamber (depth band 40–400) from the first workers, or a review of fT/devRate against the soil temperature model.

Core queen-care: the feed threshold QUEEN_FEED_LOADS × 0.5 = 0.05 is above the nanitic minim crop (0.037), so carers stick in queen-care.feed and the queen is never fed. The fungus module works around it with its own queenFeed.ts and queen-care demand 0 for Atta.

Core locomotion / nav grid: the nav cell just outside the Atta entrance is classed 'blocked-solid', so every navTo from the entrance fails ('no-route'). The fungus module escapes with a short wander (cut.clear) and a 30 s retry.

Core brood humidity hazard (brood.ts:181) reads air RH through chamberRh, giving 17 brood humidity deaths in 4 GD. I added the additive chamberRhRule hook in envAdapter.ts (listed) instead of editing brood.ts; core may prefer chamber humidity for all species.

Core hauling: brood corpses pile up in a single-chamber founding nest (22–24 'waste' items, inNest) faster than haul takes them out, which drives the hygiene hazard cascade. It was masked here once starvation stopped.

Progression: the ms-first-leaf rule requires c + p > 0, so the leaf delivery event carries LU in `c`. Succession foodC and life.ts delivery C therefore count leaf LU as food C. A leaf kind with c = p = 0, or a separate lu field, would be cleaner.
Difficulty: add diseaseMult (GDD 06) to the difficulty params block.
notesForIntegrator: Deviations from GDD 07, all documented in the code: (1) while the colony has no media/major, minims cut small fragments (minimCutTrips ≤ minims/2, halved when the substrate is supplied); (2) minims process (×2 time) and haul waste while no media works the gardens (noProcessors); (3) gardeners feed the queen from staphylae, then the pool (queenFeed.ts), because the core queen-care threshold blocks minims; (4) the queen's laying budget is held to 0 after hand-over while pool P + staphylae + (yield − queen upkeep) × 2.5 GD does not cover the brood's remaining protein plus one egg (LAY_COVER_GD and QUEEN_FL_PER_GD in balance, [EST]); (5) the hitchhiker is abstract; (6) spread distance between gardens is straight-line, not tunnel distance; (7) garden visuals are inert display items, not a renderer.

Trophic eggs: now only the first clutchCap (40) eggs are counted for the 0.7 share; a relay clutch after a loss is kept whole. This changed after the suburban-garden 2/3 and playground-park runs; suburban-garden 1 and the soak have the same hand-over and identical day rows before and after.

findings.title: A 'seeded' garden starved to ~0 GU never dies, so the colony never becomes garden-less
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/fungus/states.ts:31 (`if (g.biomass < P.deadG && s !== 'seeded') return 'dead'`); red test review.verify.test.ts 'a seeded garden starved of all substrate eventually dies'
findings.detail: nextState exempts `seeded` from the G < deadG rule, and starvation never lowers health. A seeded garden with no substrate therefore shrinks toward 0 and stays 'seeded' forever. Repro: pure steps for 20 GD at G0 0.6, subIn1Gd 0, gardeners 3 gives G < 0.1 but the state is still 'seeded'. This is the real case: after the hand-over the founding garden stays 'seeded' below 1 GU. My e2e ends at 'seeded' 0.71 -> 0.62 GU, and the implementer's r2 run also ends 'seeded' at 0.62. A starving founding garden can therefore never trigger garden-less (§6.4.9), all-gardens-lost, the queen's 3 GD reserve or the epitaph. The feed rule and the laying hold keep treating it as alive.

findings.title: Health recovery never happens in play: the 'no toxin' gate meets a leaf table where every plant is toxic
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/fungus/dynamics.ts:107 (subT <= 1e-6) with src/sim/balance/species-leafcutter.ts LEAF_TRAITS (herbage t 0.05, others 0.1-0.45); red test 'a garden fed ordinary herbage ... recovers health'
findings.detail: GDD 07 §6.4.2 gives +0.1 h/GD when i = 0, c < 0.2, fclim >= 0.8 and there is no toxin. The module's own LEAF_TRAITS give every plant kind a toxin above 0, so any real substrate has subT > 0. Repro: a garden at h 0.7, 23 °C, RH 0.9, fully supplied with LEAF_TRAITS.herbage, ends at h 0.6775 after 3 GD instead of about 1.0. Every knock (heat, an outbreak, poison) is therefore permanent, and gardens drift toward stressed/collapsing over a season. Fix one side: a toxin threshold (e.g. below rejectToxin) or toxin-free common herbage.

findings.title: Refuse workers are made nurses and feed larvae (GDD 07 §6.4.4)
findings.where: AntFlag.REFUSE is read only in src/sim/species/modules/fungus/behaviourGarden.ts; allocation.ts never excludes refuse workers; red test 'refuse workers are never made nurses and never feed larvae'
findings.detail: The GDD rule: a waste hauler becomes refuse and is 'never again assigned garden or nurse'; nestmates avoid it. Nothing outside the garden FSM reads the flag. When no waste is waiting, chooseJob returns GJ.none, the cycle ends, and the colony allocator gives the ant any task. Repro: 6 REFUSE minims, 8 larvae, 0.4 GD gives 3425 ant-ticks with task 'nurse' (expected 0). In a probe, refuse media were also reassigned to cut and forage. Fix: an additive allocator hook or a demand filter that keeps REFUSE ants off nurse and queen-care.

findings.title: Minims in a minim-only colony haul waste and become REFUSE for life with half their remaining lifespan
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/fungus/behaviourGarden.ts chooseJob (`big = media || (minor && noProcessors)`) + becomeRefuse; red test 'minims gardening ... are not turned into refuse workers'
findings.detail: The first-brood deviation lets minims do media work, including GJ.waste, whenever no media gardens. Every minim that hauls once is flagged REFUSE, its remaining lifespan is halved, and from then on it only hauls. GDD §6.4.6 stage 8 gives waste to small and full media. Repro: kit with G 1.5, W 1 and 4 minims on garden, no media; after 1 GD, 2 of 4 minims are REFUSE. In the real founding (8-14 minims, no media for a long time) this steadily removes gardeners and feeders. It is a plausible contributor to the early 'old-age' deaths in the logs (sg1b: 6 of 9 minims dead of old age by Winter 1 against a 40 GD mean lifespan; atta-soak28: 9 of 9 by day 17). I have not proven how much of that decline it explains; the 3x ageing outside on minim cut trips and scouting also contributes.

findings.title: Garden waste is put down inside the garden chamber when there is no midden and no open entrance; W drops but the waste never leaves
findings.where: src/sim/species/modules/fungus/behaviourGarden.ts startDump (`if (!p) { tryAct(... 'put-down') }`); balance WASTE_DUMP_MIN_BU declared but never used; red test 'waste taken from a garden is not left lying in a fungus chamber'
findings.detail: middenPoint returns null when the nest has no midden chamber and no open entrance. That is the state of a young nest that is closed (sealed after the hand-over, rain closure); the architect makes no midden early. The hauler then puts the garden-waste item down where she stands. Repro: entrance held sealed, W 3, 3 media gardeners, 0.25 GD gives W 0 and 6 garden-waste items lying in the garden chamber (chamberId of the room). Contamination never sees this waste and nothing ever picks it up (the report admits only the second half). The ≥25 BU-from-fungus midden rule (§5.4.6) is not applied at all.

fix:species-leafcutter.summary:
Fix round for the review of species-leafcutter. I reproduced all 7 of the reviewer's red tests. Each defect was fixed at its root cause, and all 16 reviewer tests now pass. In one of them I changed a precondition that contradicted the correct fix; the reason is written in the test file.

1. Seeded gardens now die. A starved `seeded` garden reaches dead when G < 0.1, so the colony can become garden-less and the queen's reserve, the epitaph and the diagnostics all work (states.ts).
2. Health can recover on real leaves. GDD 07 §6.4.2 says recovery needs "no toxin", but every plant in LEAF_TRAITS has some toxin. The rule now reads "no toxin" as substrate toxin at or below HEALTH_RECOVER_TOXIN_MAX (0.1, in the balance file). Ordinary herbage and clover pass; defended plants do not.
3. Garden waste is now its own job, task `haul` with subtype garden-waste, as GDD 07 §6.4.6 stage 8 and the spec ask.
   - New file behaviourHaul.ts takes over the haul entry state. When garden waste is due it does that first; otherwise it hands over to the shared haul behaviour.
   - Only small media, media or refuse workers may take waste (actions.ts). Taking waste flags the ant as a refuse worker with half her remaining lifespan; the player is affected too.
   - Minims never haul waste, even when the colony has no media.
   - Each allocation pass, ensureWasteHaulers moves refuse workers first, then small media, then media onto `haul`.
4. Refuse workers can no longer nurse or garden. Editing the colony allocator was refused by permissions, so a local guard (refuse.ts) runs twice per tick and moves any refuse worker it finds on nurse, queen-care or garden to `haul`.
5. Waste dump rule (wasteDump.ts): a midden at least 25 BU from every fungus chamber first, then the surface heap beside an open entrance, then a midden that is too close. If none exists, nobody takes the waste: it stays in W, where contamination counts it. A load that cannot reach the dump goes back into its garden's W.
6. tend-fungus now honours the secondary variant ("plant pulp" or "take waste"). The effect reads `ant.action.secondary` and `onBegin` re-times the action.
7. diag-garden now warns for a seeded garden that is short of substrate.

Minor findings, also done:
- All inline tunables are in the balance file.
- Hot paths are cached once per tick: the colony list, noCutters, noProcessors and gardener counts.
- The phorid-rate denominator now counts every laden carrier once per trip.
- A dead garden's chamber can only be re-seeded after W = 0.
- A garden whose chamber is lost now dies with a `garden-state` event and a cause.
- `GardenRecord.quarantined` is written each garden step.
- The chamber-humidity hook is chained instead of overwritten.
- Garden display lumps cannot be picked up.
- Leaf fragments a possessed ant puts down in a garden chamber join the cache.
- New playerPrompts.ts says what a possessed leafcutter should be offered by caste. It is not wired in yet; that needs a hook in the targeting code, which is outside my paths.

Viability: suburban-garden seed 1 now passes the Winter-1 bar. Workers went 9 → 9 with 43 leaf deliveries, no starvation and no stage worse than lean. Before this round the same seed lost all 9 minims to old age and failed. Only this one seed was re-run, and its founding needed the forced seal. The full bar (2 of 3 seeds on two archetypes) is still not shown.

Harness runs e2e1 and e2e2 both exited 0, and I looked at every screenshot:
- 03-castes-possessed.png (e2e2) shows the castes told apart by day in rusty brown: major with the big head on the left, media, small media, and the possessed minim in front.
- 02 shows the pale garden mass in the founding cell.

- No refuse heap appeared within the run window.

notDone: The viability bar is not met. Only suburban-garden seed 1 was re-run: it passes with leaf work, but it relied on the forced seal, and the founding was re-run with the new code because --cache-any did not reuse a snapshot. playground-park and the other seeds were not re-run (each run takes about 25-50 minutes on this loaded machine). The earlier founding failures are core issues: the queen drowned (playground-park 1), larvae flooded (suburban-garden 3), and the automatic seal never closes the 35 BU Atta shaft.

The leaf-carrying picture still does not read as a column. The first brood is all minims (2.4 mm), and minim-only colonies send at most half their minims on cut trips. A real column needs media, which come only with growth.

No refuse heap appears in the e2e window: only media haul garden waste, and the first-brood colony has none. In a minim-only colony the waste stays in the garden (W) and raises contamination until small media emerge; this follows GDD 07 §6.4.6 stage 8.

The garden stays in the founding cell, which is hot (fT about 0.3). Relocation needs a `fungus` chamber. The architect plans 2 fungus chambers at 10 or more adult workers (REQUIRED_TYPES in balance/architect.ts, not mine), and minims cannot dig. Nothing in my paths proposes an earlier fungus chamber.
The possession prompts are not wired: fungusSelfPrompt exists and is tested but is never called.
'Nestmates avoid contact with refuse workers' (GDD 07 §6.4.4) is not modelled.
Quarantine routing of waste ('straight to a midden, avoiding other gardens') is still abstract; quarantine only reduces spread.

No new render files exist under src/render/nest/species/fungus* or src/render/ants/species/atta*. The Atta morphologies already live in src/render/ants/morph/atta.ts (not mine), and the garden is drawn as display lumps.

Architect (balance/architect.ts REQUIRED_TYPES for atta-texana): 2 fungus chambers at 10 workers is the only route to a real fungus chamber. Consider asking for one as soon as the first media emerges, so the garden can leave the hot founding cell.
notesForIntegrator: Waste hauling moved from task `garden` to task `haul` (a species-specific haul behaviour that hands over to the shared haul). The species data already lists 'haul:garden-waste' as a task subtype.

The module now wraps the shared `pick-up` action check (displayGuard.ts) in the same way it already wrapped feed-larva (feedRule.ts).
The chamberRhRule hook is now chained instead of replaced, so another module can set it too.

The whole suite was not run. Only my paths and their tests were run, per the working rules. Contract changes: none (I used existing optional fields only).
Decision recorded: 'no toxin' in GDD 07 §6.4.2 means substrate toxin at or below HEALTH_RECOVER_TOXIN_MAX (0.1, an estimate). Read literally (0), no garden could recover on any real leaf.
Machine load: life.ts ran at about 5 minutes per game day, and each harness run took about 20 minutes.
